title-proc.eng: Supply, installation, configuration, support of critical Station End Equipment for approximately 218 fire stations across Ireland. The scope includes, Supply of replacement SEE hardware components, integration with existing mobilisation systems, Provision of spares, technical support, and software updates.

description-proc.eng: Limerick City and County Council on behalf of all Irish local authority fire services are contracting for the supply, installation, configuration, support and maintenance of Station End Equipment for approximately 218 fire stations across the Republic of Ireland. SEE is a mission­critical component of the IFS mobilisation and communications infrastructure. It supports the automatic dissemination of mobilisation messages, officer alerting, and integration with station systems such as station doors and lighting. The procurement forms part of the ongoing national modernisation programme for fire service mobilisation and communications. The scope includes: • Supply of replacement SEE hardware components • Integration with existing mobilisation systems • Commissioning, configuration and acceptance testing • Preventive and reactive maintenance • Provision of spares, technical support, and software updates It is the intention of the Authority to award a contract in compliance with the European Union (Award of Public Authority Contracts) Regulations 2016 (S.I. No. 284 of 2016), Regulation 32(5)(b) ­ use of the negotiated procedure without prior publication (direct award). The procurement falls outside the scope of the standard procurement regulations for the following reasons: • The primary objective of this project is to sustain existing mobilisation functionality and operational capability until forthcoming modernisation initiatives are implemented. These future programmes are expected to reshape the role of SEE within the wider mobilisation strategy. Consequently, the immediate focus is on stability, interoperability, and continuity of service, rather than introducing substantive technical change. • The SEE system is a national, mission­critical component of the Irish Fire Service (IFS)’s mobilisation infrastructure, linking 218 fire stations with control centres and local station systems. Its performance depends on tightly coupled interfaces, station­end configurations, and communication protocols that have been proven in service. • Replacing the solution at this stage would trigger a full re­engineering of these interfaces, extensive testing cycles, and the physical redeployment of hardware across all stations. While technically possible, such a change would introduce disproportionate technical difficulties relative to the limited functional gain achievable in the short term, creating significant implementation risk, extended downtime potential, and substantial additional cost for parallel integration and validation activities. • A new solution would necessitate new maintenance, monitoring, and support processes nationwide, further increasing complexity during a period when uninterrupted service is critical. By building on the existing infrastructure, the Authority avoids those disproportionate impacts, maintains proven integrations, and https://ted.europa.eu/TED Page 1/6 ensures seamless operational continuity. • This approach represents a proportionate, value­for­money, and low­risk solution aligned with the transitional nature of the wider modernisation programme. It delivers the necessary outcome efficiently while preserving operational stability of Critical National Infrastructure. The 10­year term is necessitated by the significant capital investment and technical complexity of deploying a standardised hardware platform across the 218 fire stations in Ireland. A shorter duration would fail to provide the necessary economic amortisation period for the initial high­cost deployment. This system forms a core part of how Ireland’s national emergency response systems communicate and operate together, meaning its stability and compatibility are essential to safe and effective mobilisation. Maintaining a single­provider ecosystem for 10 years ensures operational continuity, system stability, and avoids the disproportionate technical risks and costs of replacing embedded hardware and integrations part way through their lifecycle in a mission critical emergency response environment. Accordingly, the Authority considers that extending the incumbent supplier’s contract for additional SEE deliveries and associated services is the most efficient and proportionate means of achieving the required outcome, ensuring technical compatibility, minimising disruption, and safeguarding the continuity of critical operations.

title-proc.eng: Prior Information Notice market consultation Data and AI

description-proc.nld: Prior announcement – Market Consultation Data & Artificial Intelligence The Ministry of Defence of the Netherlands (Procurement Directorate COMMIT) intends to publish a market consultation on Data & Artificial Intelligence (Data & AI) in November 2026. With this prior announcement, the Ministry of Defence informs the market in advance so that interested parties can prepare their participation for the actual market consultation. Why Data & AI matters: In the coming years, Data & AI will largely determine how fast and how well the armed forces observe, decide and act. Data & AI strengthens the information position, supports military decision-making, enables uncrewed and autonomous systems and makes logistics and business operations more effective. The technology develops rapidly and specialist expertise remains scarce. The Ministry of Defence expects structural and substantial demand in the upcoming years and cannot provide all the required knowledge, capacity and innovation independently. The Ministry of Defence therefore seeks structural, Ministry-wide collaboration with the market. Scope of the consultation: The consultation covers the full Data & AI lifecycle: from governance, policy, architecture and the responsible use of AI to the design, development, deployment, scaling, operation and further development of solutions, including adoption, knowledge transfer and Data & AI literacy. The requirement spans three Key Development Areas (Decision Support Systems, Autonomous Systems and Combat Service Support) across the maritime, land, air, cyber, space, joint and business operations domains. Responses covering only part of the scope are welcome. Out of scope: The Ministry of Defence organises the following areas through other contracts: storage and compute infrastructure, information management, generic cybersecurity, transmission and connectivity, and the hiring of individual professionals. Data security, AI-specific security, running models on edge equipment and the logic of data transport do fall within scope. The consultation documentation describes these boundaries in more detail. Innovation and short-cycle delivery: The Data & AI requirement develops in weeks and months rather than years. The Ministry of Defence therefore seeks a way of working with the market based on short cycles, rapid validation and demonstrable value. Innovation forms an integral part of the work, not a separate experimental track: successful experiments and proofs of concept must move quickly to production, scaling and operation. The consultation explores how the Ministry of Defence can organise this, including access to specialist suppliers, start-ups, scale-ups and research institutions, and how co-sourcing with Ministry of Defence teams can strengthen knowledge transfer. Intended market approach: The Ministry of Defence presents its intended market approach, based on collaboration with multiple market parties in one Data & AI ecosystem. The consultation addresses, among other topics, the structure of the requirement, the contractual model, assignment and pricing models, ecosystem collaboration, the route from innovation to production, intellectual property and exit, security and sovereignty, and barriers to participation. The Ministry of Defence presents this approach as a working hypothesis and invites the market to help refine it. The Ministry of Defence welcomes constructive, well-founded input, including points for improvement, practical alternatives and an explanation of any aspects that could hinder participation. Who may participate: The consultation is open to all interested parties, Dutch and foreign, including large and small enterprises, generalist and specialist suppliers, start-ups, scale-ups, technology partners and knowledge institutions. Geographical participation and sovereignty form part of the consultation topics. How to prepare: The questionnaire includes a capability mapping and questions on capacity, security-cleared personnel, innovation and the intended contractual approach. The consultation itself is unclassified and requires no security clearance. Participants receive approximately four weeks to respond. We advise interested parties to register on Mercell in advance. Procedure and language: The Ministry of Defence announces the consultation on TenderNed and conducts it through Mercell. The documentation describes the procedure, timeline and moments for interaction with the Ministry of Defence. The documentation is drafted in English; participants may submit their questions and responses in English or in Dutch. The Ministry of Defence treats responses confidentially and shares an anonymised summary report afterwards. The Ministry of Defence uses the outcome to prepare a possible future procurement. CPV code: The contracting authority will use the following CPV code when publishing the actual market consultation: "72000000 IT-diensten: adviezen, softwareontwikkeling, internet en ondersteuning" Status: This prior announcement and the yet to be published market consultation do not constitute a procurement procedure or a (pre-)selection of economic operators. Participation creates no advantage and non-participation creates no disadvantage. No rights may be derived from this prior announcement.

description-proc.fra: Le but est la mise en oeuvre de la stratégie du 11 décembre 2020 d’informatique en nuage de l’administration fédérale (SB020 – Stratégie d’informatique en nuage de l’administration fédérale). Divisé en trois lots, ce marché sera attribué dans le cadre d’une procédure sélective conformément à l’art. 19 LMP. * Lot 1 : cloud public à portée mondiale (cloud public avec stockage des données au niveau international) * Lot 2 : cloud public avec une gouvernance des données de confiance (cloud public avec stockage et traitement des données exclusivement en Suisse) * Lot 3 : cloud privé sur site (cloud privé dont le stockage et le traitement des données s’effectuent exclusivement dans les locaux du service demandeur) Afin de répartir les risques de défaillance et de sécurité entre plusieurs prestataires, de réduire la dépendance vis-à-vis de ceux-ci et d’améliorer la sécurité d’approvisionnement, le service demandeur applique une stratégie multifournisseur. Au total, l’adjudicateur procédera à 5 adjudications (2 pour chacun des lots 1 et 2, et 1 pour le lot 3) à différents soumissionnaires, en vue de la fourniture des services cloud et des prestations associées qui font l’objet du présent appel d’offres. Afin d’atteindre cet objectif, une limitation du nombre de lots est prévue au sens de l’art. 32, al. 3, LMP. Les documents d’appel d’offres contiennent de plus amples informations à ce sujet.
description-proc.deu: Es soll die Cloud-Strategie der Bundesverwaltung vom 11. Dezember 2020 (SB020 - Cloud-Strategie der Bundesverwaltung) umgesetzt werden. Dazu wird diese Beschaffung im selektiven Verfahren nach Art. 19 BöB durchgeführt und in drei Lose aufgeteilt: * Los 1: Public Cloud «Global Reach» (Public Cloud mit globaler Datenhaltung) * Los 2: Public Cloud «Enhanced Data Governance» (Public Cloud mit ausschliesslicher Datenhaltung und -bearbeitung in der Schweiz) * Los 3: Private Cloud «On-Premise» (Private Cloud mit ausschliesslicher Datenhaltung und -bearbeitung in den Standorten der Bedarfsstelle) Um Ausfall- und Sicherheitsrisiken auf mehrere Anbieterinnen zu verteilen, die Versorgungssicherheit zu erhöhen und die Abhängigkeit von einzelnen Anbieterinnen zu reduzieren, verfolgt die Bedarfsstelle eine Mehrlieferanten-Strategie. Es werden insgesamt 5 Zuschläge (für Lose 1 und 2 je zwei Zuschläge und für Los 3 ein Zuschlag) an jeweils unterschiedliche Anbieterinnen zum Bezug von vorliegend ausgeschriebenen Cloud Services und verbundenen Leistungen vergeben. Zur Umsetzung dieses Ziels ist eine Loslimitierung im Sinne von Art. 32 Abs. 3 BöB vorgesehen. Weitergehende Informationen sind in den Ausschreibungsunterlagen enthalten.
description-proc.eng: The aim is to implement the Federal Administration's cloud strategy of 11 December 2020 (SB020 – Federal Cloud Strategy). title-proc.eng: Hermetic Thermal Gravimetric Analyser - Mettler Toledo TGA/DSC 3+

description-proc.eng: The Thermal Gravimetric Analyser (later also “TGA”) measures the change in mass of a sample as it is heated, cooled or held at a constant temperature in a defined atmosphere. Samples that are sensitive to air can be prepared and analysed under a hermetic process at a reduced pressure thus preventing their decomposition. The intended use of the TGA is for the analysis of stable solid-state materials, their synthesis studies and analysis of ALD precursors. Volatility and thermal stability are essential properties of ALD precursors. They are inherently very air sensitive, implying fully inert handling. Fully inert TGA at reduced pressure provides direct access to the key parameters of ALD precursors developed at CHEM, allowing swift feedback to our precursor development. Solid-state research focuses on the behavior of multi-metal oxides – such as battery materials – or their precursors. The Department of Chemistry and Materials Sciences has developed solid knowledge of TGA use and analysis, but we lack a device fulfilling our teaching and research needs. An automated sample loader with hermetic sample crucibles ensures consistency and minimizes errors in multi-user environment.

Helsingin kaupunki järjestää markkinavuoropuhelun, jonka tavoitteena on varmistaa potentiaalisten tarjoajien kanssa käytävien keskustelujen avulla tulevien tekonurmien tulevaan puitejärjestelyyn 2027-2028 kilpailutettavien tekonurmipinnoitteiden vaatimuksia. Ilmoittautuminen infotilaisuuteen (osanottajien nimet ja s-postiosoitteet) pyydetään tekemään viimeistään 13.11.2026 klo 16.00 mennessä sähköpostitse osoitteeseen kymp.infrahankinnat@hel.fi. Tilaisuudessa käydään yleisellä tasolla vuoropuhelua puitesopimuksen kohteesta ja sen määrittämisestä, sekä pyritään saamaan hankinnan valmistelua varten riittävä tieto markkinoiden laajuudesta, sekä toimittajien kiinnostuksesta osallistua hankintaan. Tuleva puitesopimus liittyy Helsingin kaupungin tekonurmikenttien peruskorjaushankkeisiin, joita toteutetaan vuosina 2027 ja 2028. Arvoitu uusien tekonurmipinnoitteiden tarve on 40000–50000 m2tr sopimuskaudella vuosittain. Puitesopimus sisältää tekonurmipinnoitteiden toimituksen asennuksineen myöhemmin julkaistavan puitesopimuksen hankintailmoituksen mukaisesti. Hankkeen tavoitteena on selkeyttää tekonurmipinnoitteiden valintaa ja hankintaa tuleville tekonurmikenttien rakennushankkeille huomioiden: - Tekonurmipinnoitteen tulee täyttää EU:n asetuksen mikromuovien käytön kieltämisestä - Monipuolinen tuotevalikoima eri käyttötarkoituksiin ja käyttötasoille helpottaen pinnoitteen valintaa kenttäkohtaisesti - Tekonurmipinnoitteiden hankinnan selkeyttäminen ja nopeuttaminen - Kustannustehokkuus ja tuleva volyymi - Tukea Helsingin kaupungissa toimivia jalkapalloseuroja löytämään uusia tekonurmipinnoitteita kumirouhe tekonurmien tilalle. description-proc.eng: This is a call for market dialogue. This is not an advance notice, a procurement notice or a call for tenders, and the publication of the announcement shall not start a tendering process. The City of Helsinki is organizing a market dialogue with the aim of ensuring the feasibility of the upcoming framework agreement for artificial turf coatings through discussions with potential bidders. The market dialogue is organized in two stages: - The market dialogue will be initiated with a joint information session on October 30, 2024, where the client will present the upcoming procurement to potential service providers and answer any questions. In addition, service providers are expected to present their own perspectives. - In November 2024, the client will arrange bilateral technical dialogues to survey the market players and offerings. The information session will be held using the Teams application on October 30, 2024 at 13.00 – 14.00. (UTC +2) Registration (participants' names and email addresses) for the October information session and November's company-specific technical dialogues is requested by email to kymp.infrahankinnat@hel.fi by October 25, 2024 at 16:00 (UTC +3) at the latest. Please title the email: "Artificial turf coatings framework agreement 2025-2026, market dialogue." During the session, a general level dialogue will be conducted about the subject of the framework agreement and its definition, and an effort will be made to gather sufficient information for the procurement preparation regarding the extent of the market and the service providers' interest in participating in the procurement. The aim is to receive constructive proposals from the bidders for the final preparation of the procurement, such as the options for artificial turf coatings available on the market. The future framework agreement is related to the renovation projects of the artificial turf fields of the city of Helsinki, which will be implemented in 2025 and 2026. The estimated need for new artificial turf surfaces is 40,000–50,000 m2 per year during the contract period. The framework agreement includes the delivery of artificial turf coatings with installation in accordance with the framework contract procurement notice to be published later. The goal of the project is to clarify the selection and procurement of artificial grass coatings for future construction projects of artificial turf fields, considering: - The artificial grass coating must comply with the EU regulation on the prohibition of the use of microplastics - Diverse range of product selection for different purposes and levels of use, making it easier to choose a coating for each sport field - Clarifying and speeding up the procurement of artificial turf coatings - Cost effectiveness and future volume - To support the football clubs operating in the city of Helsinki to find new artificial turf products to replace rubber infill artificial turf. Participation in the event does not bind the participant to any possible tenders or contracts. The market dialogue does not bind the city of Helsinki to implement the procurement or to start the bidding process. The market dialogue does not bind the participating suppliers to make an offer, and on the other hand, not participating in the market dialogue has no effect in a participation to a possible tender. Suppliers are not compensated for participating in the market dialogue.

description-proc.eng: Landsnet intends to enter into a negotiated procedure without prior call for competition with Hyosung Heavy Industries for the modifications to the substation at Bakki in Húsavík, pursuant to Article 53(1)(c) of Regulation No. 340/2017, on the basis that competition is absent for technical reasons and that no reasonable alternative or substitute is available in the circumstances. The technical solution for the required modifications is closely linked to the existing substation design recently developed and delivered by Hyosung. By engaging Hyosung, Landsnet can reuse and adapt this existing design and make use of Hyosung’s existing technical knowledge of the solution, thereby avoiding the need for another supplier to undertake a separate design process before equipment manufacture and implementation can commence. This is of particular importance in light of the required connection date of 1 April 2028. Landsnet only received sufficiently definite information regarding the connection requirement and its timing in September 2026. Based on Landsnet’s project schedule, an alternative procurement route involving a separate procurement of engineering design, completion of that design and a subsequent competitive procurement of the equipment would require approximately 32–36 months and would therefore not enable Landsnet to meet the required connection date. Hyosung has, in addition, agreed to give the project priority in its production schedule. The combination of reusing and adapting the existing technical design and commencing the manufacturing process without the additional design and procurement stages provides a materially shorter implementation route and a basis for meeting the required connection date. Against this background, Landsnet considers that no reasonable alternative or substitute is available that would meet the technical requirements within the available implementation period. The proposed direct award to Hyosung is therefore based on the specific technical circumstances of the project and the absence of a reasonable alternative, rather than on an artificial restriction of the procurement requirements.

title-proc.eng: 10012255-Short Term Expert Support on Sustainable and Inclusive Mobility in Colombia

description-proc.eng: ProMOVIS II, implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), supports Colombian cities in strengthening their capacities to deliver public transport systems that better serve their populations. Colombia has committed to ambitious climate targets under its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), requiring a 51% reduction in projected emissions by 2030. The transport sector accounts for approximately 45% of energy related GHG emissions nationwide, making the decarbonization of urban transport one of the country's most impactful mitigation opportunities. Despite ongoing efforts, the integration of public transport systems at local and regional levels remains insufficient, affected by the lasting effects of the pandemic, financing gaps, low digitalization, and early stage regional integration, particularly critical in metropolitan regions with high intermunicipal commuting, such as Valle del Cauca. Within this context, ProMOVIS II concentrates technical cooperation efforts on strengthening public transportation, incorporating a regional integration perspective and initially focusing its actions on Valle del Cauca. The objective is that public transport in selected Colombian cities is more integrated, inclusive and environmentally friendly, pursued through three outcomes: (1) number of people benefiting from newly created or improved public transport; (2) funds secured by selected cities to finance environmentally friendly, integrated public transport projects; and (3) number of bus operators and transport authorities that assess that professionals trained in green jobs training formats contribute positively to integrated, inclusive and environmentally friendly public transport. Through technical assistance, financing-related support, and knowledge exchange, ProMOVIS II addresses the institutional, organizational and operational challenges that limit the effective integration and sustainability of public transport systems, working closely with national and local governments, transport authorities and other stakeholders to strengthen local capacities and develop solutions that are replicable, scalable and sustainable over time.

Access to the site during the renovation phase will require coordination with the main construction contractor (details are provided after the contract has been signed). It is expected that participation in a mandatory construction site safety training (approximately one hour) will be required prior to site access. At the time of issuing this tender, the specified area within Sähkötalo is undergoing renovation. The renovation is scheduled for completion by the end of April 2027. title-proc.eng: Supply of HDR Brachytherapy System within LIFEGATE project

description-proc.eng: Cardiovascular and oncological diseases remain the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in Montenegro and the wider cross-border region. According to GLOBOCAN 2020 data, Montenegro recorded 3,184 new cancer cases and 1,765 cancer-related deaths. With the expected increase in cancer incidence, an ageing population, and existing healthcare challenges, improving early detection, diagnostics, and access to specialised treatment is becoming increasingly important. The Clinical Centre of Montenegro (CCM), as the country's leading tertiary healthcare institution, plays a crucial role in providing specialised oncology services. Through this project, CCM aims to strengthen its diagnostic and treatment capacities, introduce advanced medical technologies, and improve the quality and accessibility of cancer care. A particular focus is placed on early lung cancer detection and the improvement of radiotherapy treatment, including the application of advanced techniques such as stereotactic radiotherapy and brachytherapy. These approaches are expected to contribute to more precise and effective treatment, improved patient outcomes, and better survival rates. Brachytherapy represents an important component of the planned improvements at CCM, offering opportunities to enhance treatment efficiency and quality for patients with various malignancies, particularly cervical, prostate, oesophageal, and lung cancers. The project will also support the development of innovative digital solutions, improved cancer prevention and screening programmes, and the modernisation of healthcare infrastructure through new equipment and professional training. Through cooperation with healthcare institutions in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Clinical Centre of Montenegro will contribute to strengthening cross-border collaboration, exchanging medical expertise, and promoting common standards in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. Ultimately, the project aims to improve access to modern oncology services, enhance treatment outcomes, and strengthen the long-term capacities of the Clinical Centre of Montenegro, benefiting patients in Montenegro and the wider cross-border region.

title-proc.eng: Technical Assistance for Climate Change Adaptation Planning and Improved Response

description-proc.eng: This project foresees implementation of activities focused on climate adaptation measures addressing both, river and torrential floods separately, taking into account their distinct characteristics and specificities, as outlined below: River Floods 1. Renewal of the Hydrological Information System (HIS) for the main sub-basins in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including flood events from 2010 to the present. 2. Analysis of the impact of existing reservoirs on the water regime, with proposals for improving the management of high-water waves and enhancing water retention during dry periods. 3. Development of guidelines for flood protection of agricultural land. 4. Preparation of the manual “Living with Floods”, providing an overview of necessary measures and best practices for flood risk management. Torrential Floods 1. Development of a cadastre of torrential basins, including a sensitivity model based on existing erosion maps. 2. Preparation of a study on increasing basin water retention capacity through measures aimed at reducing runoff and sediment transport, accompanied by a catalogue of applicable interventions.

title-proc.eng: Rfp Event Venue – EIT Urban Mobility Community Days 2027

description-proc.eng: By the present procurement procedure, EIT Urban Mobility, hereinafter being referred to as “EIT UM”, is aiming to identify an Event Venue, hereinafter being referred to as “The Venue” or “Venue, based in Brussels to host our Community Days 2027 events and provide catering, furniture, staff, branding and audiovisual support. This document, along with its annexes, constitutes a Request for Proposal (RFP) issued by EIT Urban Mobility for a potential procurement of services in the field of events. Community Days 2027 will comprise a series of strategic meetings and stakeholder engagement activities. Community Days: The 2027 edition of EIT Urban Mobility Community Days will take place in Brussels (Belgium) on 16th and 17th March 2027. EIT UM intends to gather all partners from different European locations under one roof and organize a 2-day event designed just for them. Exact timings are still to be decided. It will be held as an in-person by invitation-only event, and we are expecting to have approximately 250 participants. RAPTOR Summit: The RAPTOR Cities session is planned as a dedicated meeting within the wider Community Days event, bringing together representatives of cities and startups/SMEs participating in the RAPTOR programme. Integrating the Summit into Community Days allows RAPTOR participants to meet in person to exchange experiences, discuss pilot results and lessons learned, and explore opportunities for continuation and replication, while also participating in and benefiting from the broader Community Days programme. Supervisory Board Meeting: The Supervisory Board is the highest governing and oversight body of the EIT Urban Mobility legal entity. As part of its mandate, the Board is responsible for supervising the activities, performance, and strategic direction of the KIC Legal Entity, as well as overseeing the work of the Management Team. City Club Advisory Group Meeting: The City Club Advisory Group (CCAG) brings together representatives of Leading Cities within the EIT Urban Mobility community to provide strategic advice and a city perspective on EIT Urban Mobility’s activities, priorities and future direction. The group provides a structured forum for cities to exchange experiences and best practices, discuss common urban mobility challenges and emerging priorities, and contribute insights that can inform the development of EIT Urban Mobility’s activities and engagement with public authorities.

title-proc.eng: Market dialogue for the procurement of WAN Services for Norway's Foreign Service Missions

description-proc.eng: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs invites potential suppliers to a market dialogue prior to the planned procurement of WAN for Norway ́s foreign stations. The objective of the market dialogue is to examine what possibilities exist in the market in addition to receiving input on what we ought to focus on in the coming procurement. We particularly encourage tenderers to give feedback on what can be seen as exclusive, competitive and/or price driven in a coming procurement. The current agreement for WAN services expires in 2028. A new procurement process must therefore be initiated to ensure that a new contract is in place and that new connections are implemented before the existing agreement expires. The foreign stations currently mainly use local WAN connections. Some locations use satellite services as the primary connection due to local infrastructure conditions and/or geographical location. Satellite services are generally used as secondary connections and are also expected to be in the future. SAT services are subject to a separate market dialogue and tenderers are encouraged to respond to this if the service can be provided.
